mainTopic: Paying the fourfold or fivefold fine (תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה) when the thief's slaughter or sale also breaks another איסור. The focus is slaughtering on יום הכפורים and whether you can get both a punishment and a payment.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a thief's sale counts as a sale because he really transfers ownership. Next comes the משנה's rule that a thief who slaughters on יום הכפורים pays ארבעה וחמשה. The גמרא asks how this can be, since that act brings מלקות, and it answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds לוקה ומשלם but not מת ומשלם. A ברייתא seems to show רבי מאיר making a thief pay even for slaughtering on שבת. The גמרא explains that the ברייתא speaks of a thief who had an agent slaughter for him. פסוקים teach that an agent's slaughter counts, and רב אשי explains why this is not the agent doing 'more' than the thief. The חכמים who exempt are רבי שמעון, who holds that an unfit slaughter is not a slaughter. A שבת slaughter counts as unfit for him because he follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, who forbids food made on שבת on purpose, based on 'כי קדש הוא לכם'. The amud ends with רב אחא and רבינא arguing whether מעשה שבת is forbidden from the Torah or only by the רבנן, and a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A limited sale still counts as a sale
steps.stepSummary: The earlier discussion ends here. Even though the thief's sale had some limitation, he still transfers ownership this way, so it counts as a מכירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, since he transfers ownership to him in this way, it is a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a discussion from just before this point. It rules that the thief's sale counts as a real sale, so he pays ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the sale was not complete or normal. The answer is that what matters is a real transfer of ownership (הקנאה) to the buyer. If that happened, it is a מכירה for this law.

keyTerms.meaning: transfers ownership
a sale
even so; even though

steps.whatToRemember: For תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה, any sale where the thief truly transfers ownership counts, even if it is unusual.

phrases.english: Even so,
since he transfers ownership to him in this manner,
it is considered a sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי כֵּיוָן דְּקָא מַקְנֵי לֵיהּ בְּהָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sale with a limitation is still a מכירה, because ownership really passes to the buyer.

steps.title: The משנה: stealing and slaughtering on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה about a thief who slaughters the animal on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] If one stole and slaughtered on יום הכפורים, etc. (he pays ארבעה וחמשה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that a thief who slaughters on יום הכפורים still pays the fourfold or fivefold fine. This is surprising, because the slaughter itself is a sin with its own punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement fast day
slaughtered
etc.; the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: If he stole and slaughtered on Yom Kippur, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the משנה: he still pays four or five times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief who slaughters on יום הכפורים pays ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: Why pay if he gets lashes?
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering on יום הכפורים carries מלקות. Since the rule is that a person is not both flogged and made to pay, how can the משנה make him pay?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Why should he pay? True, there is no death penalty for working on יום הכפורים, but there are at least lashes. And we hold that a person is not both lashed and made to pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It points out that slaughtering on יום הכפורים brings מלקות, and normally you cannot get both lashes and a payment for one act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of אינו לוקה ומשלם says one act brings only one punishment: either lashes or payment, not both. Working on יום הכפורים is punished by כרת and מלקות, not death by בית דין. So the lashes should cancel the payment, which goes against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: why?
granted; true that
execution, the death penalty
lashes
one is not both lashed and made to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up יום הכפורים with שבת. Working on שבת can bring the death penalty, but on יום הכפורים the punishment by בית דין is only מלקות.

phrases.english: They say: Why?
Granted that there is no execution,
there are at least lashes;
and we hold that one is not lashed and also pays!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the thief pays ארבעה וחמשה for slaughtering on יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughtering on יום הכפורים brings מלקות. The accepted rule אינו לוקה ומשלם should then cancel the payment.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can be both lashed and made to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי מאיר, who says a person is lashed and also pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It says the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who disagrees with the usual rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not change the rule אינו לוקה ומשלם for everyone. It only says the משנה follows a תנא who holds לוקה ומשלם. For him, lashes and payment can go together.

keyTerms.meaning: whose view is this?
a תנא, quoted here as holding לוקה ומשלם
he is lashed and also pays

phrases.english: They say: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: one is lashed and pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא (הא מני).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה goes against the accepted rule אינו לוקה ומשלם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds לוקה ומשלם.

steps.title: Then why is slaughtering on שבת exempt?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי מאיר, then a thief who slaughters on שבת should also pay. But the משנה exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי מאיר, then even if he slaughtered on שבת he should pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If רבי מאיר lets a person be punished and pay at once, the שבת case should be the same as יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts a thief who slaughters on שבת, because שבת carries the death penalty. If רבי מאיר allows two punishments for one act, he should require payment on שבת too. Saying the משנה is רבי מאיר seems to create a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: if
The weekly day of rest

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir,
then even if he slaughtered on Shabbat [he should pay]!
phrases.notes: The משנה (74b) says he is exempt if he slaughtered on שבת, because that act carries the death penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֲפִילּוּ טָבַח בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's view should require payment for slaughtering on שבת too, but the משנה exempts it.

steps.title: A possible answer: lashes and payment, but not death and payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way out. Maybe רבי מאיר holds לוקה ומשלם but not מת ומשלם, and the next step will test this idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: he holds that one is lashed and pays, but he does not hold that one is put to death and pays...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the שבת problem. The wording וכי תימא shows it is about to test this answer against a ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that רבי מאיר makes a difference between two kinds of punishment. Lashes can go together with payment, but the death penalty cancels payment. That would explain why יום הכפורים (lashes) brings payment but שבת (death) does not.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you will say; brings in an answer that will be tested
put to death and also pays
he holds / he does not hold

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase וכי תימא brings in an answer that the גמרא immediately challenges in step 7. Here the answer survives: steps 8–10 explain the ברייתא away, so רבי מאיר holds לוקה ומשלם but not מת ומשלם.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
he holds 'one is lashed and pays,'
but he does not hold 'one is put to death and pays';

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לוֹקֶה וּמְשַׁלֵּם אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the קשיא of step 5. The next lines go on to test it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction (lashes compared with the death penalty).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר allows any punishment to go together with payment, so the שבת case should require payment too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: רבי מאיר allows lashes together with payment, but not death together with payment. This suggestion is about to be tested.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר makes a death-penalty thief pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 6. A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר saying that a thief who slaughters on שבת or for עבודה זרה still pays ארבעה וחמשה, even though those acts carry the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי מאיר really not hold that a person can be killed and also pay? But a ברייתא teaches: If someone stole an animal and slaughtered it on שבת, or stole and slaughtered it for עבודה זרה, or stole an ox that was sentenced to stoning and slaughtered it, he pays four or five times. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from step 6 by quoting a ברייתא where רבי מאיר makes a thief pay even though his act carries the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering on שבת and slaughtering for עבודה זרה are both sins punished by death. If רבי מאיר still makes the thief pay ארבעה וחמשה, it looks like he holds מת ומשלם after all. That would knock out the way step 6 explained why our משנה exempts the thief who slaughters on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
Being liable to death and also having to pay for the same act
The fourfold or fivefold payment a thief owes for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox
An ox sentenced to stoning; no one may benefit from it
They exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people in this sugya. Right now the ברייתא looks like the thief himself did the slaughtering. The next step will say that someone else slaughtered for him.

phrases.english: And not?!
phrases.notes: He means: does רבי מאיר really not hold מת ומשלם, the way step 6 suggested?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If he stole and slaughtered on שבת;
if he stole and slaughtered for idol worship;
if he stole an ox that is to be stoned and slaughtered it –
he pays four or five times,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the Sages exempt him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion in step 6 that רבי מאיר holds לוקה ומשלם but not מת ומשלם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר does not hold מת ומשלם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר requires payment even for slaughtering on שבת or for עבודה זרה, which are capital sins. That suggests he does hold מת ומשלם.

steps.title: The ברייתא speaks of a thief who had someone else slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא cannot be taken at face value. Several אמוראים explain that it speaks of a thief who had another person slaughter the animal for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Put that ברייתא aside, because it was explained like this. רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and some say רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש, and רבי אבין, רבי אלעא and the whole group said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It speaks of someone who slaughters through another person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 6 by explaining that the thief in the ברייתא did not slaughter the animal himself. He had someone else do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an agent did the slaughtering, the agent is the one who broke שבת or served עבודה זרה. The thief committed no capital sin, so there is no death penalty to block the payment. This means the ברייתא is no proof that רבי מאיר holds מת ומשלם.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave that one aside; that source does not mean what it seems
It was stated about it; an explanation was given
And some say it; a different version of who said it
The group, here the students of רבי יוחנן
Through another person, an agent

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer saves the idea that רבי מאיר holds לוקה ומשלם but not מת ומשלם. It also opens the next question: how can the thief pay for something someone else did?

phrases.english: They say: Leave that one aside,
for it was stated about it:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: רבי יעקב said that רבי יוחנן said,
and some say רבי ירמיה said
that רבי שמעון בן לקיש said,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אָבִין וְרַבִּי אִלְעָא וְכֹל חֲבוּרָתָא
phrases.english: and רבי אבין, רבי אלעא and the whole group
say in the name of רבי יוחנן:
It speaks of one who slaughters through another person.
phrases.notes: The thief told someone else to slaughter it, so the other person did the שבת or עבודה זרה sin, not the thief.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: בַּר מִינַּהּ דְּהַהִיא, דְּהָא אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the ברייתא is about a thief who slaughtered through an agent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thief slaughtered himself, so רבי מאיר seems to hold מת ומשלם.
steps.terutzMaskana: An agent slaughtered, so the thief committed no capital sin. The ברייתא says nothing about מת ומשלם.

steps.title: How can one person sin and another person pay?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if the agent did the slaughtering, why should the thief owe the four or five times payment?
steps.simpleTranslation: But can it be that this one sins and that one becomes liable?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 8. It asks how the thief can be liable for an act that someone else did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person is responsible for his own actions, and he is not liable when someone else does the wrong. So step 8 creates a new problem. If the agent did the slaughtering, why should the thief pay ארבעה וחמשה?

keyTerms.meaning: But can it be? Introduces a sharp, surprised question
Sins
Becomes liable

phrases.english: But can it be that this one sins and that one becomes liable?!
phrases.notes: "This one" is the agent who slaughtered. "That one" is the thief who stole the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא speaks of slaughtering through an agent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person is not normally liable for a sin someone else commits, so the thief should not pay for the agent's slaughtering.

steps.title: רבא: The פסוק links slaughtering to selling, which always involves another person
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that ארבעה וחמשה is different. The פסוק puts slaughtering next to selling. Selling always involves another person, so slaughtering through another person also counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Here it is different, because the פסוק says, "and slaughters it or sells it." Just as selling is done with another person, so too slaughtering can be done through another person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 9. He shows from a פסוק that for ארבעה וחמשה, the thief is liable even when someone else does the slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions slaughtering and selling together. You cannot sell without a buyer, so selling always involves another person. Because the two are linked, slaughtering done by an agent also makes the thief liable. This is a special rule of the תורה for this payment, not a general rule that one person pays for another's sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different
For the פסוק says
Selling
Slaughtering
Just as ... so too; a comparison learned from the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר makes the thief pay because an agent slaughtered, so the thief committed no capital sin. The thief is still liable for the agent's slaughtering because the פסוק links slaughtering to selling, and selling always involves another person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the explanation from step 6 standing: רבי מאיר holds לוקה ומשלם but not מת ומשלם.

phrases.english: רבא said: It is different here,
for the verse says: "and slaughters it or sells it" –
just as selling is through another person,
so too slaughtering can be through another person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning from a פסוק: putting slaughtering next to selling makes slaughtering through an agent count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One person cannot be liable for another person's act, so the thief should not pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: For ארבעה וחמשה, the תורה links slaughtering to selling, so slaughtering through an agent makes the thief liable.

steps.title: Two more sources that include the agent
steps.stepSummary: The schools of רבי ישמעאל and חזקיה each learn from a different word in the פסוק that slaughtering through an agent makes the thief owe ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: the word "or" comes to include the agent. The school of חזקיה taught: the word "in place of" comes to include the agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more teachings from the פסוק. Both agree with רבא that a thief who has an agent slaughter for him still pays ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא learned this from slaughtering being placed next to selling. These two schools reach the same result from other words in the same פסוק: "או" and "תחת". The rule that an agent's slaughter counts now rests on three separate sources.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
To include (an extra case)
Agent, someone acting on another person's behalf
In place of

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Or" comes to include the agent.
phrases.notes: From שמות 21:37, "and slaughters it or sells it."

phrases.english: The school of Chizkiya taught:
"In place of" comes to include the agent.
phrases.notes: Same פסוק: "five cattle in place of the ox, and four sheep in place of the sheep."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives other sources for רבא's rule that slaughtering through an agent counts.
steps.raayaObject: A thief who slaughters or sells through an agent owes ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words "או" and "תחת" in the פסוק, as taught by the schools of רבי ישמעאל and חזקיה.

steps.title: Can an agent create liability the thief himself would not have?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges this: a thief who slaughters on שבת himself does not pay, so how can he pay when his agent does the slaughtering?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objected: Is there anything where, if a person does it himself, he is not liable, but if his agent does it, he is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא attacks the answer from step 8. According to it, the thief pays when an agent slaughters for him, but not when he slaughters on שבת himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An agent normally stands in the place of the person who sent him. He should not be able to create more liability than the sender himself would have. Here the agent's act seems to make the thief pay, while the thief's own act would not.

keyTerms.meaning: Objected to it (a sharp challenge)
Is there anything at all…?
Is liable, must pay

phrases.english: Mar Zutra objected to it:
Is there anything
where if he does it himself, he is not liable,
but if an agent does it, he is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea that the thief pays when his agent slaughters.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא speaks of slaughtering through an agent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An agent cannot create more liability than the sender would have for doing the act himself.

steps.title: The thief himself is liable but gets the bigger punishment
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that a thief who slaughters on שבת himself really is liable to pay. He only escapes payment because he faces the death penalty, under the rule קם ליה בדרבה מיניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: There, it is not because he is not liable. Rather, he is subject to the greater punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that the thief in the שבת case is not truly free of liability. Something else blocks the payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the thief slaughters on שבת himself, he deserves death, and a person who deserves death and payment for one act gets only the death penalty. When an agent slaughters, the thief did not break שבת, so no death penalty blocks the payment. The agent adds nothing; he only removes the obstacle.

keyTerms.meaning: He receives the greater punishment and is spared the lesser one
There (in that case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This separates "not liable" from "liable but blocked by a bigger punishment." That difference answers מר זוטרא.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מִיחַיַּיב הוּא,
phrases.english: There, it is not because he is not liable,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case where the thief slaughters on שבת himself.

phrases.english: rather, because he is subject to the greater punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines why the thief does not pay: it is not a lack of liability but the rule קם ליה בדרבה מיניה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A thief who slaughters on שבת is simply not liable, so his agent should not make him liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is liable, but the death penalty blocks payment. With an agent there is no death penalty, so payment applies.

steps.title: Then why do the רבנן exempt the thief?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the ברייתא is about slaughtering through an agent, what reason do the רבנן have to exempt the thief?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is about one who slaughters through another person, what is the reason of the רבנן, who exempt him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the answer from step 8. It now looks at the רבנן, who argue with רבי מאיר in that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי just explained that with an agent there is no death penalty, so nothing should block payment. The פסוקים also include an agent's slaughter. So why would the רבנן exempt the thief? This sets up the next answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Through another person
Who exempt

phrases.english: But if it is about one who slaughters through another person,
what is the reason of the Rabbis, who exempt him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בְּטוֹבֵחַ עַל יְדֵי אַחֵר מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן דְּפָטְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the agent explanation is defended for רבי מאיר, the גמרא tests it against the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא speaks of slaughtering through an agent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With an agent there is no death penalty and the פסוקים include the agent, so the רבנן's exemption has no clear reason.

steps.title: The חכמים are רבי שמעון: an unfit slaughter is not counted as slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים who exempt the thief are רבי שמעון. He holds that a slaughter that does not make the meat usable is not called שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Who are the חכמים? They are רבי שמעון. He said that a slaughter that is not fit does not count as a slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14. The חכמים who exempt the thief are really רבי שמעון, and he has his own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption is not about the agent at all. רבי שמעון holds that if the slaughter does not make the meat usable, it is not legally a slaughter. So the thief never 'slaughtered' in the way the פסוק requires for ארבעה וחמשה.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughter that is not fit, meaning it does not make the meat usable
It is not called a slaughter; it does not count legally
They say; introduces an answer or comment by the scholars

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not say the animal was never killed. He says that legally this killing does not count as the 'slaughter' that creates the payment of ארבעה וחמשה.

phrases.english: They say: Who are the Rabbis? It is Rabbi Shimon,
who said: a slaughter that is not fit
is not called a slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the opinion to a specific תנא with his own known rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to have no reason to exempt the thief once slaughter through an agent counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים are רבי שמעון. He exempts because an unfit slaughter is not legally a slaughter.

steps.title: But slaughtering on שבת does make the meat kosher
steps.stepSummary: עבודה זרה and an ox sentenced to stoning do make the meat forbidden. But a משנה rules that slaughtering on שבת is valid, so how can רבי שמעון call it unfit?
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: It makes sense for עבודה זרה and an ox that is to be stoned, since those are slaughters that are not fit. But on שבת it is a fit slaughter! As a משנה teaches: one who slaughters on שבת or יום כיפור, even though he is liable to death, his slaughter is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 15. It says the 'unfit slaughter' reason works for two of the cases in the ברייתא but not for the שבת case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat from עבודה זרה or from an ox sentenced to stoning is forbidden to use, so those slaughters really are unfit. But a משנה in חולין says a שבת slaughter makes the meat kosher, even though the person who did it deserves death. So רבי שמעון's rule should not exempt the שבת thief.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for; grants one part before challenging another
An ox sentenced to be stoned (for killing a person); its meat is forbidden
Liable with his life; deserves the death penalty
His slaughter is valid; the meat may be eaten

phrases.english: They say: It makes sense for idol worship
and an ox that is to be stoned,
since that is a slaughter that is not fit;
but on Shabbat, it is a fit slaughter!
As we learned: one who slaughters on Shabbat or on Yom Kippur,
even though he is liable with his life,
his slaughter is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: בִּשְׁלָמָא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְשׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון exempts the thief in all three cases because each is an unfit slaughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that a שבת slaughter makes the meat kosher, so the שבת case is a fit slaughter and רבי שמעון's rule does not cover it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, who disagrees with that משנה and treats a שבת slaughter as unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: He holds like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says רבי שמעון follows a different תנא, רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, who forbids what was done on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in חולין that makes a שבת slaughter valid is not everyone's opinion. According to רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, food prepared on שבת on purpose is forbidden. So for him a שבת slaughter is also 'not fit', and רבי שמעון's rule covers the שבת case too.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like; he follows the view of
A תנא whose view on food made on שבת is stricter

phrases.english: They say: he holds
like Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the opinion to another תנא who disagrees with the cited משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שבת slaughter is always fit, as the משנה in חולין says.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, for whom a שבת slaughter is unfit, so the שבת case is also an unfit slaughter.

steps.title: The משנה about cooking on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה where רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's view appears. First come רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה on eating food cooked on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: one who cooks on שבת, if by mistake it may be eaten, if on purpose it may not be eaten; this is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: if by mistake, it may be eaten after שבת ends; if on purpose, it may never be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the source for רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's view. It begins quoting a משנה with several opinions about food cooked on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר forbids the food only when it was cooked on purpose. רבי יהודה is stricter: even food cooked by mistake must wait until after שבת, and food cooked on purpose is forbidden forever. These two views prepare the ground for רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's opinion in the same משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: By mistake; without knowing it was forbidden
On purpose; knowing it was forbidden
After שבת ends, on Saturday night
Forever; never

steps.confusionAlert: This part of the משנה does not yet show רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's own words. It is only the beginning of the source that leads up to his view.

phrases.english: As we learned: one who cooks on Shabbat,
if by mistake, it may be eaten;
if on purpose, it may not be eaten;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: if by mistake,
it may be eaten after Shabbat ends;
if on purpose, it may never be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts quoting the source for the view of רבי יוחנן הסנדלר mentioned in step 17
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנא, רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, who forbids food prepared on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תרומות about one who cooks on שבת

steps.title: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר: on-purpose cooking on שבת is forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר rules that food cooked by mistake on שבת may be eaten by others after שבת but not by the cook. Food cooked on purpose may never be eaten by anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says: if he did it by mistake, others may eat it after שבת, but he may not. If he did it on purpose, it may never be eaten, not by him and not by others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it started in the last step and reaches רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's opinion. This is the proof it was looking for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, something made on purpose on שבת is forbidden to eat forever. שחיטה on שבת is the same kind of serious שבת violation as cooking, so meat slaughtered on purpose on שבת can never be eaten. That is a slaughter that does not make the meat usable, which is why רבי שמעון can say the thief pays no ארבעה וחמשה.

keyTerms.meaning: For others, meaning people other than the one who cooked
But not for him, the one who did the cooking
Neither for him nor for others

steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the loop from step 17: רבי שמעון can follow רבי יוחנן הסנדלר and treat an on-purpose שבת slaughter as one that does not make the meat usable.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar says:
If done by mistake, it may be eaten after Shabbat ends
by others, but not by him;
if done on purpose, it may never be eaten,
not by him and not by others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quote begun in step 18
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן הסנדלר treats an on-purpose שבת act as making the food forbidden forever, so רבי שמעון can follow him
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about eating food cooked on שבת

steps.title: What is רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's strict ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוחנן הסנדלר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יוחנן הסנדלר gets his ruling from. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making food on שבת is a sin, but it is not obvious why the food itself should become forbidden to eat. The גמרא wants a source for that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason
of Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for forbidding food made through שבת desecration

steps.title: רבי חייא compares food made on שבת to קדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא learns from 'כי קדש הוא לכם' that just as קדש may not be eaten, food made through שבת desecration may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught at the entrance of the נשיא's house: 'And you shall keep the שבת, for it is holy to you.' Just as קדש is forbidden to eat, so too things made on שבת are forbidden to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching of רבי חייא that compares שבת to קדש, based on the פסוק calling שבת 'holy'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls שבת 'קדש'. Something consecrated to the בית המקדש may not be eaten by an ordinary person. So רבי חייא says that food made through a שבת violation also may not be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, taught from a פסוק
The house of the נשיא, the leader of the Jewish people
Something holy, consecrated to the בית המקדש
Things produced through forbidden work on שבת
Forbidden to eat

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiyya expounded
at the entrance of the house of the Nasi:
"And you shall keep the Shabbat,
for it is holy to you"
just as a holy thing is forbidden to eat,
so too things made on Shabbat are forbidden to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְדָרֵישׁ רַבִּי חִיָּיא אַפִּיתְחָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'כי קדש הוא לכם' compares שבת products to קדש, which may not be eaten

steps.title: Then benefit should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the comparison further: קדש is also forbidden for any benefit, so food made on שבת should be forbidden for benefit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as קדש is forbidden for benefit, then things made on שבת should also be forbidden for benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how far the comparison goes. If שבת food is like קדש, it should match קדש completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדש is forbidden not only to eat but also for any use or benefit. If the comparison is complete, food made on שבת could not be used at all, not even sold or given to an animal. The גמרא asks whether that is really true.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Forbidden for any benefit or use

phrases.english: If so, just as a holy thing is forbidden for benefit,
so too should things made on Shabbat be forbidden for benefit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of the comparison made in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between מעשה שבת and קדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, benefit should also be forbidden, just like קדש

steps.title: 'לכם' means benefit is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The word 'לכם' teaches that food made on שבת stays yours for benefit. Only eating is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'to you': it shall be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the same פסוק: the word 'לכם' limits the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לכם' means 'yours', so the food still belongs to you for use and benefit. The comparison to קדש applies only to eating, not to benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us
It shall be yours

phrases.english: The verse says: "to you"
it shall be yours.
phrases.notes: So you may still use it or benefit from it. Only eating it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעשה שבת is like קדש in every way, including benefit
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לכם' shows benefit is allowed; only eating is forbidden

steps.title: Maybe even a mistaken act forbids the food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, based on the comparison to קדש, food made by mistake on שבת should also be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think it is forbidden even if done by mistake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another possible way to stretch the comparison: maybe it applies even when the person did the work by mistake. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדש is holy no matter how it came about. So one could think that food made through a mistaken שבת act is also forbidden like קדש. That would not fit רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, who allows others to eat it after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought

phrases.english: One might think: even if done by mistake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a second limit on the comparison from step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between מעשה שבת and קדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison could cover mistaken acts too, which would contradict רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's leniency for שוגג

steps.title: 'מחלליה מות יומת' limits it to on-purpose acts
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק says one who desecrates שבת is put to death. That only happens for an on-purpose act, so the prohibition applies only to מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Those who desecrate it shall surely be put to death.' I told you this about one who acts on purpose, not by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the continuation of the same פסוק. This completes the source for רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death penalty applies only to someone who violates שבת on purpose. Since the פסוק links the 'קדש' comparison to that kind of violator, the food is forbidden forever only in a case of מזיד. This matches רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's split between שוגג and מזיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who desecrate it, meaning שבת
He shall surely be put to death

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, food made through an on-purpose שבת violation is like קדש: it is forbidden to eat forever ('כי קדש הוא'). Benefit is still allowed ('לכם'), and the rule applies only to מזיד ('מחלליה מות יומת'). So an on-purpose שבת slaughter does not make the meat usable, which fits רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: The verse says: "Those who desecrate it shall surely be put to death"
phrases.notes: שמות 31:14, the same פסוק as before

phrases.english: I told you this about one who acts on purpose,
and not about one who acts by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting phrase in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even a mistaken act would make the food forbidden like קדש
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an on-purpose act, which carries the death penalty, makes the food forbidden like קדש

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about the level of the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue over whether the ban on מעשה שבת comes from the Torah or from the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One says the ban on things made through שבת desecration is from the Torah. The other says the ban is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a new disagreement about how strong the ban on food made on שבת really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the גמרא learned the ban from a פסוק through רבי חייא's reading. Now two אמוראים argue about that. One says the ban is truly from the Torah. The other says the Torah does not forbid it, and only the רבנן do.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
Something produced by doing a forbidden act on שבת
From the Torah (Torah-level law)
From the Rabbis (rabbinic-level law)

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a ban is Torah-level or rabbinic affects how strict we are when there is doubt, and it shapes the rest of this סוגיא.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ban on food made through שבת desecration, which the last few steps learned from the פסוק.

phrases.english: one said: the product of a Shabbat act is forbidden by Torah law,
and one said: the product of a Shabbat act is forbidden by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the limits of רבי חייא's derivation, the גמרא brings a dispute over whether that derivation is truly Torah-level.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One אמורא holds that מעשה שבת is forbidden מדאורייתא, and the other holds it is forbidden only מדרבנן.

steps.title: The source behind each side
steps.stepSummary: The Torah-level view relies on רבי חייא's reading. The rabbinic view reads 'קדש הוא' as saying only the day is holy, not what is made on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is from the Torah learns it the way we said, from רבי חייא's reading. The one who says it is rabbinic points to the פסוק 'it is holy.' 'It' (the day) is holy, but the things made through it are not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side reads the same פסוק, 'כי קדש הוא לכם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah-level view keeps רבי חייא's comparison: just as קדש may not be eaten, food made on שבת may not be eaten. The rabbinic view focuses on the word 'הוא' (it). The day itself is holy, but what is made on it is not compared to קדש. So the Torah does not forbid eating it, and the ban is only from the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: As we said (pointing back to what was already taught)
The פסוק says
It (the day itself) is holy
But what is made through it is not holy

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same פסוק. They do not argue about the פסוק itself, only about which word in it to stress.

phrases.english: The one who says it is Torah law: as we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי חייא's reading of 'כי קדש הוא לכם' (steps 21–25).

phrases.english: And the one who says it is rabbinic law:
the verse says: "It is holy"
it is holy, but its products are not holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind each side of the dispute from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah view: the comparison to קדש forbids eating. Rabbinic view: 'הוא' limits the holiness to the day itself, so the Torah does not forbid what is made on it.

steps.title: Opening a question that works well for the Torah-level view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a 'בשלמא' question. Something makes sense for the Torah-level view, which suggests a problem for the rabbinic view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says it is from the Torah, it is because of...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It says something fits well with the Torah-level view, and the question against the other view comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בשלמא' means 'it makes sense according to X,' and it is usually followed by 'but according to Y, why...?' Here the amud stops at 'אמטו' (because of). The full reason and the challenge continue on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (opens a question against the other view)
Because of (start of the word אמטו להכי, 'for this reason')

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says it is Torah law,
it is because of...
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here and picks up on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After each side's source is explained, the גמרא begins testing the two views against each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: Most likely the rabbinic view (מעשה שבת דרבנן), since 'בשלמא' grants the Torah-level view first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something can be explained by the Torah-level view, and the גמרא will ask how the rabbinic view explains it. The details continue on the next amud.
